newsitem.title: UK: UK shares little changed, awaiting Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: UK shares little changed, awaiting Wall Street.

text.p: UK shares were little changed ahead of the opening of Wall Street, where shares were expected to open higher.
At 1323 GMT, the benchmark FTSE 100 was up 3.8 points to 4,634.7, yet decliners led advancers 57 to 41. Ex-dividends took almost three points off the index.
Dealers attributed the market's lacklustre performance to profit-taking after the recent surge, but said there appeared to be more upside if Wall Street could hold opening gains.
Some said they were disappointed that unexpected news of the 23-billion-pound proposed merger between Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc didn't give more of a lift to the broader market.
The deal, said one London dealer, "has helped the sector, but people are still a bit uneasy and we're seeing a bit of profit-taking, especially in financials".
Financial stocks led the blue chip index to a record level of 4,646.0 on May 9.
Shares in Grand Metropolitan soared 88-1/2p to 603-1/2, having set a record at 613 earlier.

Guinness shares jumped 96-1/2p to 613, having risen as high as 625 earlier as investors cheered the merger, which would create the world's seventh-largest food and drinks company with a market capitalisation of over 23 billion stg.
The deal lifted others in the food and drinks sector, including Cadbury Schweppes Plc up 17p to 546 and Allied Domecq Plc, up 17-1/2p to 446.

But after rising for nine straight sessions and 17 out of the past 18 trading days a pull back of at least 50 points is likely over the next few days, Kirit Shah, stock strategist at Sanwa International, said.
"There are a few more uncertainties creeping into the market like (Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon) Brown's first budget," Shah said.
In other trading, shares in British Telecom Plc slipped 4p to 447-1/2, hit by fears it will be in Brown's budget as one of a long list of companies that will be subject to a windfall tax.
